stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model benefits from Ollama's MLX engine, featuring new native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: The rapid expansion of data centers, driven by generative AI, is a major infrastructure trend.
The massive electricity demand from these new data centers threatens to reverse decades of air quality improvements in regions like Texas.
The reliance on gas-fired power sources to meet this demand is highlighted as a primary driver of increased pollution.

stories.title: Xbox wants you to pay 24 to 40 cents per hour to stream games you already bought
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Xbox is reportedly introducing time-based, a la carte streaming charges for games users have already purchased.
These hourly fees (ranging from 24 to 40 cents) are an additional cost on top of the original game purchase price.
This represents a significant shift in digital game ownership and consumption models.

stories.title: RIP BioWare: EA shuts down storied RPG studio after over three decades
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: BioWare, a long-standing RPG studio, has been shut down by its parent company, EA.
The closure involves significant layoffs, affecting approximately 400 employees.
A planned sequel to the Mass Effect series has been canceled as part of the restructuring.

stories.title: The End of Consensus Research?
stories.author: Martijn de Vos
bullet_points: The paper addresses the long-standing, fundamental problem of consensus in distributed computing, crucial for state machine replication (SMR).
Researchers leveraged AI to aid in the discovery of 'A-greement,' a novel consensus protocol.
A-greement is presented as a significant advancement, offering superior performance for geo-replicated state machines compared to current state-of-the-art solutions.

stories.title: Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI Installs a Credential Stealer and Backdoor
stories.author: abhisek
bullet_points: A critical security vulnerability was found in the LiteLLM library (version 1.107.0) hosted on PyPI.
The compromise involves the installation of a credential stealer and a backdoor.
This represents a significant supply chain attack risk within the AI/ML development ecosystem.

stories.title: Eight Bits of Trust; eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds
stories.author: scotthelme.co.uk via pims
bullet_points: eMudhra's Certificate Authority (CA) keys were reportedly compromised.
The breach was allegedly achieved in milliseconds, indicating a severe vulnerability.
This represents a critical security failure in a major digital trust infrastructure.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the active AI research ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model from Meta.
It is featured on Hugging Face Benchmarks, indicating community interest and performance tracking.
The model falls under the text-generation pipeline, confirming its use case in generative AI.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains, including transformers and text-generation.
The presence of Llama and Facebook tags indicates relevance to major large language model developments.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local, persistent operation, enabling multi-step tasks and tool calling on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Tesla says customers can add their own vehicles to the robotaxi fleet next year — will it happen?
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Tesla has set a timeline for allowing customers to integrate their personal vehicles into the robotaxi fleet.
The announcement came during the company's third-quarter earnings call.
The development relates to Elon Musk's long-standing promises regarding unsupervised autonomous driving capabilities.

stories.title: Meta to create a new class of shares to fund AI push
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta is launching a new class of non-voting shares to finance its aggressive AI initiatives.
The capital raised will also support potential acquisitions and employee compensation.
Trading for these specialized shares is scheduled to commence in 2027.

stories.title: Meta says it would’ve made over $22 billion if it didn’t have to pay a child safety settlement
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta reported that a child safety settlement cost the company $9.89 billion in Q3.
The company stated its operating income would have been $22.89 billion without the settlement payment.
This highlights the significant financial impact of regulatory and safety compliance issues on major tech firms.

stories.title: PHP: The three letters that shut down sites all over the internet today
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Critical vulnerabilities were discovered in the PHP programming language, a foundational technology for much of the internet.
The bugs, linked to AI, have caused major outages or issues on high-profile sites like Wikipedia, 4chan, and DeviantArt.
The scope of the issue is significant, potentially affecting any website built using PHP, including WordPress.

stories.title: OpenAI's latest AI models are coming to Google Cloud and Antigravity
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: OpenAI's advanced AI models (GPT 6.1, Astra, Sol, Luna) are being integrated into Google Cloud.
This signals a major expansion of OpenAI's ecosystem availability across major cloud providers.
The partnership highlights the increasing trend of multi-cloud AI deployment.

stories.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
stories.author: Mayur Naik
bullet_points: Introduces 'Environment Duels,' a novel agentic benchmark for evaluating frontier LLMs.
The benchmark tests LLMs not only as solvers but also as creators within interactive environments.
It models the real-world co-evolution of LLMs by having models create environments for competitors to solve.

stories.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
stories.author: Calvin Xiao
bullet_points: Introduces Quant-Arena, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLM agents in end-to-end quantitative trading research.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks by testing LLMs on the entire research loop (hypothesis -> signal -> testing -> iteration), not just isolated components.
Focuses on the practical application of LLMs in finance, moving beyond simple code generation to complex, iterative strategy development.

stories.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
stories.author: Mike Zheng Shou
bullet_points: Introduces Multimodal Embodied Agents (MMEAs) as a unified framework bridging computer-use agents and robotic systems.
MMEAs are defined as goal-directed systems that integrate multimodal task reasoning with physical action and feedback loops.
The research addresses the fundamental shift in capabilities and challenges when an agent transitions from purely digital interaction to physical embodiment.

stories.title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical privacy vulnerability in Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) by integrating Differential Privacy (DP).
Identifies a key limitation in current private alignment methods: their reliance on dense reward parameterizations, leading to high estimation error.
Proposes a novel approach—Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation—to mitigate the prohibitive scaling of error bounds with model size.

stories.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
stories.author: Jianfei Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'LongZero,' a method to enhance long-context reasoning in LLMs without requiring extensive, expensive training data.
Addresses the critical bottleneck in RL-based LLM improvement: the scarcity and high cost of generating long, diverse, and verifiable training data.
Proposes a novel 'RL from zero data' approach to overcome dependencies on external corpora or stronger teacher models.

stories.title: Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation with Preference Feedback
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy vulnerability in Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) by incorporating Differential Privacy (DP).
Identifies a key limitation in current private alignment methods: they assume dense reward parameterizations, leading to high estimation error.
Proposes a novel approach for Differentially Private Sparse Reward Estimation to overcome the prohibitive scaling issues related to model size.

stories.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
stories.author: Mayur Naik
bullet_points: Introduces 'Environment Duels,' a new dynamic agentic benchmark for evaluating frontier LLMs.
The benchmark tests LLMs not only as solvers but also as creators of interactive environments.
It models the real-world co-evolution of LLMs by having them interact with and learn from each other's outputs.

stories.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
stories.author: Calvin Xiao
bullet_points: Introduces Quant-Arena, a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLM agents for end-to-end quantitative trading research.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks, which only test isolated components (formulas, code) rather than the full research loop.
Aims to determine if LLMs can autonomously complete the iterative process of hypothesis generation, signal implementation, and strategy validation in finance.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Cloudflare's 27B multimodal decision model, Clef, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This expands the accessibility of powerful, large-scale multimodal models within the Ollama ecosystem.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, 'Beam', available via Ollama.
Beam is specifically engineered for complex tasks like software engineering, reasoning, and agentic workflows.
The model is currently offered free of charge through Ollama Cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of local AI models within a cloud environment.
The integration allows AI agents to run safely on Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure, deployable AI agent solutions.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new decision models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution for answering questions with probabilistic outcomes.
The models are designed to handle yes/no questions, choices, and scoring based on textual input.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Flying Roadsters can’t lift Tesla’s flat Q3 revenues
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Tesla reported flat revenue of $28.0 billion for Q3 2026.
Despite the Roadster demo hype, Tesla's net income fell by 4 percent to $1.7 billion.
The earnings report highlights a divergence between product excitement (Roadster) and current financial performance.

stories.title: Bose acquires Skullcandy to help it reach a wider audience
stories.author: Andrew Liszewski
bullet_points: Bose has acquired competitor Skullcandy in a strategic industry move.
The acquisition aims to expand Skullcandy's market reach using Bose's advanced technology.
Bose's proprietary features, such as head-tracking spatial audio and ANC, will be integrated into Skullcandy products.

stories.title: Tesla profits drop 43% in Q3
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: Tesla experienced a significant 43% drop in profits during the third quarter.
The company's energy storage division also saw a contraction in Q3 2026.
The news signals potential headwinds or shifts in Tesla's core business performance.

stories.title: Report: Musk ordered Starlink slowdown in Ukraine, then blamed it on Trump
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A report alleges Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of Starlink services in Ukraine.
The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) is cited as the source reporting Musk's alleged order.
Both Musk and Donald Trump have publicly denied any such order.

stories.title: Does opting out of smart TV tracking work? Research finds “suspicious” traffic.
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Research suggests that opting out of smart TV tracking may not be fully effective.
The study found evidence of 'suspicious' data traffic even when users attempt to opt out.
The research author indicates that operating systems are unlikely to discard the collected user data.

stories.title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
stories.author: Jeong Joon Park
bullet_points: PhysiCalWorld addresses a critical limitation in world models: the inability to infer underlying physical properties (mass, friction, damping) from limited visual observations.
The proposed method calibrates these missing physics factors, preventing world model predictions from drifting toward simple empirical priors in new environments.
This research advances the field of embodied AI and simulation by enabling more physically grounded and robust predictive modeling.

stories.title: BatchBench: Benchmarking AI Robustness to Batch Effects and Domain Shift in Biomedical Images - A JUMP Cell Painting Leaderboard
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces BatchBench, a new leaderboard designed to benchmark AI robustness in biomedical imaging.
Addresses the critical issue of domain shift, where AI models fail when tested on data from different experimental conditions.
Focuses on evaluating the performance of AI systems against batch effects in complex biomedical image analysis.

stories.title: AtomicRL: Atomic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Liang Lin
bullet_points: The paper introduces AtomicRL, a novel approach to improve Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robotic manipulation.
It addresses limitations in existing VLA-RL methods, specifically delayed and biased credit assignment caused by sparse rewards.
AtomicRL aims to overcome performance bottlenecks arising from imbalanced mastery across subtasks in long-horizon skills.

stories.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
stories.author: Jun Xu
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in sequential recommender systems where computational resources are allocated uniformly.
Identifies that items in a user's history require varying amounts of computation to stabilize prediction quality.
Proposes 'Item-Level Adaptive Recursion' to dynamically allocate computational budget based on item importance.

stories.title: BatchBench: Benchmarking AI Robustness to Batch Effects and Domain Shift in Biomedical Images - A JUMP Cell Painting Leaderboard
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces BatchBench, a new leaderboard specifically designed to benchmark AI robustness in biomedical imaging.
Addresses the critical issue of domain shift, where AI models fail when tested on images acquired under different experimental conditions.
Focuses on evaluating the performance of AI systems against batch effects and domain shifts in complex biomedical datasets.

stories.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
stories.author: Jianfei Chen
bullet_points: The paper proposes 'LongZero' to enhance long-context reasoning in LLMs without relying on extensive, expensive, or scarce training data.
It addresses the limitations of traditional Reinforcement Learning (RL) for LLMs, which typically requires large amounts of high-quality, long, and verifiable data.
The method appears to introduce a novel 'RL from zero data' approach, circumventing the dependency on external corpora or stronger teacher models.

stories.title: Did the Problem Actually Get Harder? Testing LLMs on Paired P and NP-Complete Problems Hardened by Adversarial Multi-Agent Rewriting
stories.author: Shubhashis Roy Dipta
bullet_points: Introduces P2NPCBench, a new benchmark designed to test Large Language Models (LLMs) on the boundary between P and NP-Complete (NPC) problems.
The benchmark pairs NPC problems with their polynomial-time (P) counterparts, forcing models to reason about complexity rather than just recall solutions.
Addresses a limitation in existing LLM benchmarks, which often fail to distinguish between problems based on their inherent computational complexity.

stories.title: GoiBERT: Compact Vietnamese Language Models via Two-Stage Knowledge Distillation
stories.author: Huynh Dai Nhan Tran
bullet_points: Introduces GoiBERT, a family of compact Vietnamese language models (26M and 49M parameters).
Addresses the deployment cost and size issues of current large Vietnamese pre-trained encoders.
Utilizes a two-stage knowledge distillation process using complementary teacher models.

stories.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Praneeth Vepakomma
bullet_points: Introduces Uniform Diffusion Language Models (UDLMs) for text generation via iterative denoising of corrupted tokens.
UDLMs face a more challenging training objective than Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs) because they condition on potentially unreliable context.
Despite being more FLOP-intensive to train, UDLMs demonstrate superior downstream reasoning performance.

stories.title: What the Author Wrote, What the Agent Reads: Silent Cue Loss in Enterprise Document Ingestion
stories.author: Pradeep Kumar Misra
bullet_points: Identifies a critical, often overlooked information loss point in enterprise document ingestion pipelines.
The loss occurs when converting complex documents (like Word/PDF) into tokens for AI agents, specifically losing authorial intent conveyed through text formatting.
This silent loss leads to AI agents making confidently incorrect decisions rather than simply failing to process data.

stories.title: Agent Behavior Maps: Locating Agents by What They Would Do, Without Running Them
stories.author: Masafumi Oyamada
bullet_points: Introduces 'Agent Behavior Maps' to characterize LLM agents based on their potential actions.
Allows for comparing agent behavior using centered action log-likelihoods without needing to run new environment rollouts.
Demonstrates that geometric distances derived from the map correlate well with measured trajectory KL divergence across multiple models.

stories.title: CVE-2026-107891: musl libc: multiple integer overflow in regcomp, possibly leading to incorrect allocation sizes and out-of-bounds heap writes
stories.author: openwall.com via dzwdz
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-107891) has been identified in musl libc.
The flaw involves multiple integer overflows within the regcomp function.
Exploitation could potentially lead to incorrect memory allocations and out-of-bounds heap writes.

stories.title: Multi-tier model routing on GKE: balancing Gemini 4 Argon reasoning depth with latency and cost
stories.author: olivi-eh
bullet_points: Focuses on building a high-throughput model routing gateway on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).
Addresses the practical challenge of balancing reasoning depth (Gemini 4 Argon) against latency and cost.
Demonstrates a practical deployment strategy by routing requests across different model tiers (Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 3.8 Flash, local Gemma 4).
